videos.title: Kurdecha vs Tsvetkov: Where the Match Is Won or Lost | EvW27
videos.summary:
Kurdecha vs Tsvetkov at East vs West 27 (EvW27): where this super heavyweight match is won or lost.

Alex "Polish Viking" Kurdecha (#9) meets Georgi "Grizzly" Tsvetkov (#10) in Budapest, and to me this match is rigidity against fluidity. Kurdecha is one of the biggest humans in the sport. He has the longer lever, the bigger hand and the high ground in the setup. Tsvetkov has one of the best top rolls in the world. The rigidity and endurance in his hand and wrist have pushed Devon Larratt and taken the fight to Kamil Jablonski.

The way I see it, this match is Kurdecha to stop and Tsvetkov to finish. Tsvetkov has to go aggressive off the go, take centre and take control. As long as his wrist stays rigid and his pronation holds, it's his to win. If Kurdecha cracks the wrist or drops the pronation, the pendulum swings hard his way, because the bigger hand and the wider technical range start to come to life.

I expect an absolute war, and I have Tsvetkov as the slight favourite from the centre. I think he has the stronger peak force. Kurdecha has more options, though: the open-arm top roll, the King's move and the press finish. In the end it comes down to one question. Can Tsvetkov remain rigid?
